questions.stem: The student wants to compare the curviness of the two rivers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.html: The high-sinuosity Luni River in India is curvier than the low-sinuosity Embarras River in Canada.
The Embarras River’s ratio of stream length to valley length, also known as sinuosity, is greater than that of the Luni River.
In both the Embarras and the Luni rivers, curviness is determined by comparing stream length to valley length.
By comparing the stream lengths of the Embarras and Luni rivers to their valley lengths, one can calculate their curviness, or sinuosity.
